classifications.rationale: Classification authorities, agency personnel, and the receiving agency must follow internal training, protection, referral, and decision procedures, but the agency retains responsibility for making the later classification determination rather than being ordered to reach a specified outcome.
classifications.evidence: That agency shall decide within 30 days whether to classify this information.

classifications.rationale: The President presently limits what information is eligible for classification and fixes a default ten-year declassification timetable, directly governing classification status rather than merely requesting later policy development.

classifications.rationale: The segment presently establishes exemptions, marking duties, waiver rules, and classification treatment that directly determine the protected status and required handling of covered information.
classifications.evidence: Information assigned a level of classification under this or predecessor orders shall be considered as classified at that level of classification despite the omission of other required markings.

classifications.rationale: The President presently prohibits classification or reclassification in specified circumstances and conditions when requested or compiled information may be classified, directly restricting the classification status available to such information.
classifications.evidence: Information may not be reclassified after it has been declassified and released to the public under proper authority.

classifications.rationale: Although the segment also directs agencies to create challenge procedures, it presently establishes who may perform derivative classification without original authority and imposes binding marking duties, directly governing authority and classified-information handling.
classifications.evidence: Persons who only reproduce, extract, or summarize classified information, or who only apply classification markings derived from source material or as directed by a classification guide, need not possess original classification authority.

classifications.rationale: The President presently assigns originating-agency status and orders automatic declassification of qualifying historical records on fixed deadlines; later administration implements those already-prescribed legal-status changes.
classifications.evidence: all classified information in such records shall be automatically declassified no longer than 25 years from the date of its original classification

classifications.rationale: Agency heads and review authorities receive discretionary power to propose, approve, reject, or revise exemptions through an internal notice-and-appeal process; the segment does not itself select particular information for exemption or dictate a particular later outcome.
classifications.evidence: An agency head may exempt from automatic declassification under paragraph (a), above, specific information

classifications.rationale: The President requires agency plans to mandate a specified later declassification result—at least 15 percent of affected records within one year—so the legally consequential status change must be produced later by agency action.
classifications.evidence: the agency declassify at least 15 percent of the records affected by this section no later than 1 year from the effective date of this order

classifications.rationale: The Secretary of State is assigned discretion to decide when negotiations should begin; this is an internal authority assignment and does not itself modify a treaty or require a predetermined legal result.
classifications.evidence: The Secretary of State shall determine when the United States should commence negotiations
